# SortBy

Sorts the elements of an array in ascending order of a key that a lambda gives for each.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
SortBy(items, callback)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to sort, which is left unchanged. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `callback` | function | A lambda of exactly one parameter, which receives the element; its result, of any type, null included, is the key the element is sorted by. A lambda of any other number of parameters, or a value that is not a lambda, null included, is a runtime error. |

## Returns

Array. A new array holding the elements of items in ascending order of their keys. Never null.

## Remarks

The lambda is called exactly once for each element, in order, before any key is compared. It is given the elements the array holds when the call starts. Keys are compared as `Sort` compares values, and keys of different types never cause an error: null comes first, then booleans, numbers, strings, arrays, objects and functions. Booleans sort false before true, numbers by value, and strings by their UTF-16 code units, so case counts. The sort is stable: elements whose keys compare equal keep their original order.

## Example

`SortBy([{"n": 3}, {"n": 1}], x => x.n)` returns `[{"n": 1}, {"n": 3}]`.
